title: "The NSE gain ... a mixed result at all three lead times" is false at 1 day ahead, and "not lost skill" sits beside a fall in NSE
text: "The NSE gain ... a mixed result at all three lead times" is false at 1 day ahead, and "not lost skill" sits beside a fall in NSE. Where: Report p.16 (4.8), p.26 (conclusion 6), p.27 (Limits and the "Weather forecast" row of Table 8.1), p.28 (Next steps 2); short_report.md (Table row); Professor_QA p.15 (G4); Project_Guide p.33. The slides ("mixed at 2 and 3 days", slide 13), the key figure (marks "mixed" only at 2 and 3 days) and `key_figure.json` say 2 and 3 days, so the documents disagree with each other. Truth: `forecast_input.json` `gain_rule.wqaF_sub_against_wqa.l1.nse`: median 0.693 against 0.767 (gain -0.074), higher in 4 of 12 basins (lower in 8), Wilcoxon p = 0.79, every single training lower (`value_of_the_forecast.by_lead.l1.nse.difference_by_seed` -0.037, -0.029, -0.066); `outcome_full` itself says the forecast closes "-256%, 38% and 39% of the NSE gap (a negative share: the forecast model is below lstm_wqa)". The stored label "mixed" is the rule's catch-all (seeds say one thing, p is not small); it is not a statement that the 1-day change is a gain. Correction: "median NSE falls at 1 day (0.77 to 0.69; lower in 8 of 12 basins) and rises at 2 and 3 days (0.38 to 0.53 and 0.25 to 0.45; 'mixed' by the rule of 4.2: higher in 8 and 9 of 12 basins)". Same places: limit "a moved operating point, not lost skill" (report p.16, slide 11, Q&A H6 p.18, guide p.32) to the warning scores (CSI 0.358 against 0.337; average precision +0.065, interval +0.006 to +0.126; `value_of_the_forecast.operating_points.l1`) and say that the NSE at 1 day is lower; NSE has no warning level to move.

title: "Real time" and "a service could expect" for a retrospective substitution; the sentence the rule asks for is missing
text: "Real time" and "a service could expect" for a retrospective substitution; the sentence the rule asks for is missing. Where: Report p.1 (finding 2: "48% when Stage IV, the real-time radar product, replaces it") and p.14 ("the real-time figure to quote for this network, trained on AORC, is about 45% to 48%"); Slides 10 (title "...or 48% in real time"), 12 and 13 ("48% in real time"); Overview p.1 ("48% the same in real time, Stage IV radar"); Project_in_Plain_Words p.1 ("48% with real-time radar"); Project_Guide p.31 ("a service could expect 45% to 48%, not 51%"); Professor_QA H1 p.16 ("the figure to quote for a service is 45% to 48%"). The report nowhere says in so many words that this is a retrospective check on the test years and not a service (Q&A H10's trap comes closest). What the test is (`stage4_realtime.json`): Stage IV hours substituted for AORC on the issue days of the 611 onsets, in networks trained on AORC; no network trained on Stage IV; false warnings on days without an onset not tested (`honesty_points[0]`, `[1]`); the one-hour delay only imitated by dropping the last hour(s). `honesty_points[4]` and `review_aorc_rain_to_midnight.json` `not_checked[3]`: whether the Iowa Mesonet archive holds first postings or later gauge-corrected versions "was not established; 'real-time' for Stage IV is the builder's and the roadmap's assumption". No document carries that caveat (grepped). Correction: add to 4.6, and one line to guide p.31 and Q&A H1: "This is a check on the test years: Stage IV hours from an archive (whether first-posted or later corrected is not established) put in place of AORC at forecast time in networks trained on AORC. It is not a running service." Replace "in real time" by "with Stage IV, a real-time product" in slide titles, overview and plain-words page; "a service could expect" by "a service with these inputs might reach about".

title: "Independent AI reviewers checked every script" is wider than the review records
text: "Independent AI reviewers checked every script" is wider than the review records. Report p.1 and p.28 (section 9), p.3 (Check 2: "Each experiment script was additionally checked by its own independent AI reviewer"); slides 1 and notes; Project_Guide p.33, 36-37 (the guide counts Stage IV as its "fourth experiment" inside "four reviews of 130 listed checks"); Professor_QA G1 p.14; short_report.md. No review record covers the following (the four reviews ended by 02:28 on 8 October; `check_stage4_realtime.py` was written at 00:11 and the `11_key_figure.py` / `13_uncertainty.py` extension at 08:50-08:51): (a) `check_stage4_realtime.py`, the script behind 294 / 48% / 90% / 275 / 255, quoted in every document of the set; `review_aorc_rain_to_midnight.json` recomputed a smaller substitution on 171 of the 611 onsets (86-95 hits against 92 with AORC) and lists "Stage IV was not tested for the other 440 onsets" as not checked; (b) `check_onset_rain_clock.py` (the 35% / 46% shares of 4.6 and 4.8): "outside this review" (`review_rain_to_midnight.json` `not_checked`); (c) the 8 October extension of `13_uncertainty.py` and `11_key_figure.py` to the new sets (the 51% (41% to 61%), 39% (28% to 48%), 37% (27% to 46%) ranges): "not examined" (`review_forecast_input.json` `not_checked`; E1 round 2: "still not extended"). I checked all three myself and they hold (Stage IV counts recounted from the stored `per_onset` list, 294 / 313 / 114, 32 onsets lost and 13 gained; I did not rerun the substitution, which needs 16 GB of Stage IV files; my own 4,000-draw bootstrap of the stored forecasts: 41.5% to 61.7%, 27.9% to 48.4%, 27.2% to 46.0% against the documents' 41-61, 28-48, 27-46; clock shares re-derived from the stored means: 18 / 35 / 46%), but that is a critic's check, not the independent review the sentence claims. Correction: "Each of the four training experiments (E1, E1b, E3, E2) was recomputed by an independent AI reviewer agent; the Stage IV test on all 611 onsets, the rain-clock diagnostic and the resampling ranges of the new sets were checked by their builder only (the E1b review recomputed a smaller Stage IV substitution on 171 onsets)."

The correction asked for in M7 is a wording correction: REVIEW_WORDING in s0_summary.py now names the final critic agent and this file for those four items. What the critic did not repeat is listed in not_checked (the reduction of the raw Stage IV archive to the stored series is the main one).

title: The rain clock covers 63 hours, not '48 hours'
text: The rain clock covers 63 hours, not '48 hours'. Report p.13 ('Of the rain in the 48 hours around the 611 flood onsets, 35% fell between about 09:00 and midnight of the issue day, filed under the next day and so hidden from the model; 18% fell before 09:00 and 46% falls on the target day'), the docstring of code/check_onset_rain_clock.py and the 'what' of results/onset_rain_clock.json say 'the rain of the 48 hours around the forecast - the issue day t and the target day t+1'. The four windows the script sums (and the critic's own code, d4_rain_clock.py, reproduces) are 09:00 (t-1) to 09:00 (t) [24 h; what the Daymet table holds for day t], 09:00 (t) to 24:00 (t) [15 h], 00:00 (t+1) to 09:00 (t+1) [9 h] and 09:00 (t+1) to 24:00 (t+1) [15 h]: 63 hours, from 09:00 on the day before the issue day to midnight at the end of the target day. The shares 18 / 35 / 46% and the mean amounts 6.5 / 12.6 / 8.5 / 8.1 mm are right for these windows; only the words '48 hours' are not (and '18% fell before 09:00' means within the 24 hours up to 09:00 of the issue day). Correction: 'the rain of the 63 hours from 09:00 on the day before the issue day to midnight at the end of the target day' (the same in the docstring and the 'what' of the results file if they are regenerated).
